deep.reconstruction:
This folio has no mathematics. It is a strip of archival paper. It carries a pencil cross-reference in the upper right, 'with Add Ms a 94 18 (24)'. Below that is a one-line handwritten assessment: 'All statements made are proved. Stops abruptly.' A printed margin notice reads 'Do not write on this margin.' Along the bottom is a ruled row with a few stray marks (a '#'-like sign and an 'f'/integral-like squiggle). The handwriting and the archival format suggest a note by a later reader or cataloguer (possibly G. N. Watson, or whoever sorted the papers), not by Ramanujan.

The note describes the manuscript it accompanies, i.e. the surrounding pages of item 18(24). That manuscript is a short, fully proved piece on integral representations of the digamma function. It stops abruptly at a bare section heading '3.' on the next page.

For context, the content being assessed (on the previous and next pages) is as follows.
- Relation (4): for p, q, r > 0, ∫_0^1 (x^{p-1}/(1-x) - r x^{q-1}/(1-x^r)) dx = ψ(q/r) - ψ(p) + log r. This is proved by regularising with (1-x)^{s-1}, using Beta integrals and letting s → 0.
- Relation (5): apply (4) with p = c + a b^ν, r = b, q = bc + a b^ν, so that q/r = c + a b^{ν-1}. Summing over ν = 0..n telescopes to ψ(a/b + c) - ψ(a b^n + c) + (n+1) log b.
- Relation (6): let n → ∞ with b > 1. Since ψ(t) - log t → 0, the limit is ψ(a/b + c) - log(a/b).
- Special cases (7)-(9) give 1 - γ = ψ(2) for a = b = 2, 3, 3/2 with c = 1. For example, (7) is 1 - γ = ∫_0^1 (x^2 + x^4 + x^8 + ...)/(1 + x) dx.
- Section 2 applies the same lacunary-sum trick to the Frullani-type integral ∫_0^1 (x^{p-1} - x^{q-1})/log x dx.
